full_judgment:
5. The proceedings, as has been stated before, originate from a spacial statute, namely under section 14 of the Arbitration Act. A decree was passed in terms of section 17 thereof which says that after a judgment it pronounced in terms of section 17 a decree shall follow. An appeal lies against such a decree on limited grounds. An "Order" dismissing an application for restoration of an ex-parte decree passed under suction 17 is not a "decree' but an "Order". Section 39 of the Arbitration Act mentions 5 kinds of "Orders" under the said Act against which appeal shall lie. it specifically says that appeal shall lie from no other "Order". An "Order" dismissing an application for restoration of an ex-parte decree passed under section 17 is not among then. Therefore no appeal lies under the Arbitration Act against an "Order" dismissing an application for restoration of an ex-parte decree passed under Section 17. 

 7. Mr. A. K. M. Shafiqur Rahman has cited the case of Belayet Hossein and another vs. Md. Abu Taher and others, 32 DLR (AD) 231, where provision for appeal in a specific, statute, namely the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act was considered. It was held that under clause (12) of section 96 of the said Act the appeal was limited to the decree for pre-emption only and the proceeding in respect of which appeal is to be preferred must be a suit. No appeal lies under the Slate Acquisition and Tenancy Act against an order dismissing an application under Order 9 rule 13 C.P.C. for motoring a proceeding under section 96 of the sail Act decreed ex parte. The reasons given are, firstly, that time order of refusal to set aside the ex pate decree is not a decree and, secondly, that the order was passed in a proceeding which was not a suit. Mr. Shafiqur Rahman submits that following the same reasoning the special statute involved in the instant case, namely, the Arbitration Act should be looked into to see whether any provision for appeal has been provided in the special statute itself against an order dismissing an application under Order 9, rule 13 C.P.C. for restoration of an ex parte decree passed under section 17. I am of the opinion that the ratio deaden& of the case just cited applies on all fours in the instant ease.
